title: KV cache key redesign + TTL sweep simulator for conservative rollout
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Prefix-based KV caching can save substantial token cost but is brittle when incorrect keys or overly-aggressive TTLs evict hot prefixes. We need an automated, conservative approach that recommends cache-key shapes and TTL schedules, simulates hit-rate and cost delta, and supports safe staged applies with automatic rollback triggers.

Objective: Build a TTL sweep simulator and cache-key recommendation flow that produces actionable configs (key templates + TTL policies) together with quantitative safety signals used by the rollout orchestration. Deliverables: 1) a simulator that models prefix popularity distributions, write/read skew, and mutation patterns; 2) a scoring rubric for candidate keys and TTLs (cost-savings vs. risk); 3) an apply plan API that performs staged rollout with circuit-breaker rollbacks; 4) observability panels and alerting for rollout health and regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest historical request traces and output per-prefix hit-rate forecasts and token-cost delta estimates
Recommendation engine produces ranked candidate cache-key templates and TTL values with a safety score for each candidate
Apply plan API supports staged rollout percentages, time windows, and automatic rollback when hit-rate or error budget regressions exceed configured thresholds
End-to-end integration test demonstrating a controlled rollout in a sandbox cluster with synthetic traffic and automatic rollback on regression
Dashboards show per-prefix hit-rate, eviction rate, token-cost change, and rollout stage with alert rules wired to the rollback circuit-breaker
tasks: Design simulator input schema and modeling assumptions
Implement trace ingestion and prefixization utility (supporting existing log format)
Model components: prefix popularity sampler, TTL decay model, write-mutation invalidation model
Build recommendation scoring function (cost-savings, hit-rate confidence, instability risk)
Expose recommendation API and CLI to emit proposed config bundles
Implement staged apply controller that integrates with runtime feature flags and rollout service
Add observability: Grafana panels, SLO checks, and PagerDuty runbook entries
Create end-to-end integration test harness and run a canary rollout in staging
design_decisions: Simulator will operate on sampled traces (1-5% sampling) to bound compute costs and approximate distributions
Use a conservative prior for new prefixes (Laplace smoothing) to avoid overestimating hit-rate on sparse keys
TTL sweep will generate geometric TTL candidates (e.g., 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s) rather than arbitrary values to simplify rollout logic
Rollout controller will prefer percentage-based stage increases (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with minimum observation windows between steps
Automatic rollback thresholds: drop in prefix hit-rate > 5% absolute OR token-cost increase > 10% OR error budget consumption crossing configured SLOs
testing_plan: Unit tests for prefixizer and TTL decay math
Synthetic workload tests that emulate bursty and long-tail prefix distributions
Chaos test: introduce write-heavy mutation events to validate invalidation behavior
Integration test: deploy recommendation and rollout controller to staging with telemetry and validate rollback triggers
Performance test: ensure simulator can evaluate 24h of sampled traces for a medium-sized tenant within 30m compute time
monitoring_and_metrics: Token cost delta (baseline vs trial) aggregated per tenant
Number of automatic rollbacks and reason codes
SLO indicators: avg latency, 95th token latency, error rate
rollback_plan: Immediate unilateral rollback by controller if automatic thresholds breached
Manual rollback via console for edge cases with audit log and a short freeze window
Post-rollback analysis job that compares pre/post metrics and writes a regression report to the incident thread
If repeated false positives occur, add a grace factor and increase minimum observation window
notes: Trade-off: sampling traces reduces simulator cost but may under-represent rare hot prefixes; mitigated via targeted full-trace replays for candidates with high potential savings
We deliberately avoid recommending multi-key sharding strategies in the first iteration to reduce runtime injection complexity
Consider future integration with Optimize engine to automatically suggest quantization/batching knobs alongside TTL changes
Prototype showed a 12% token-cost reduction for sketched workloads with negligible latency impact when TTLs tuned conservatively
